seed.title: fix(prepaint): keep form controls in restored snapshots

state_transition_sequence: user produces visible state V through normal interaction
stage W persists a representation of V under write-side policy P_w
a boundary passes (navigation, reload, time, or another actor)
stage R reads the representation back under read-side policy P_r and presents V' to the user
cause_abstraction.failure_mechanism: P_w and P_r disagree about which parts of V survive the round-trip, so user state is silently lost or altered; per-stage tests pass because no test executes the full write-boundary-read sequence
cause_abstraction.seed_instance: capture preserved form controls (P_w) while the mount-time sanitizer removed them (P_r); capture.test.ts and sanitize.test.ts each passed

rejected_seed.reason: cause is value-domain (truthiness as presence); sibling search from it would collapse into grepping for truthiness checks, which is exactly the pre-registered similarity-degeneration stop condition

mutations.description: an event that normally follows the sequence end (commit, write completion) is moved between two interior transitions
a read started before a write is applied after it; a version or time boundary is inserted between write and read

the transition is performed by a different actor than the one that wrote the state (system reset path, concurrent caller) under a policy the original actor's path enforces but the new actor's path skips

sibling_surface_selection.method: surfaces were enumerated by state role - places where user state makes a persistence or lifecycle round-trip with a transform on one side (tx step/compensation lifecycle, local-first storage load/save/version-reset, local-first cache/sync ordering)

similarity_degeneration.check: no grep, token, or embedding similarity against the seed diff was used to pick targets; none of the three scenarios shares code shape with the seed fix (sanitizer allowlists) - they share only the abstracted sequence with one operator applied
similarity_degeneration.note: the pre-registered stop condition was not triggered; the experiment ran to completion

scenarios.derivation: seed sequence with the terminal event (commit) reordered into the middle of a running step; commit() checks status but not isStepRunning
scenarios.oracle_ref: packages/tx/README.md "After commit": transaction becomes immutable; types.ts TxStatus lifecycle
scenarios.hypothesis: a transaction committed while a step is in flight is later rolled back by that step's failure, executing compensations after commit

scenarios.derivation: seed sequence with the read (initial storage load) started before the user's write but applied after it; CacheManager.updateWithData has no staleness guard and executeSyncPromise lacks the mutationVersion guard that replace() declares for background results
scenarios.oracle_ref: packages/local-first/src/sync-manager.ts replace() expectedMutationVersion guard declares that a user mutation must not be overwritten by an older concurrent async result
scenarios.hypothesis: a replace() completing while the initial load is in flight is reverted when the older loaded value is applied to the cache

scenarios.derivation: seed sequence with a version boundary between write and read and the re-seed performed by the system reset actor; every other write path (replace, patch - including drafts built from initialData) validates against the schema, the version-reset branch saves and returns initialData unvalidated
scenarios.oracle_ref: packages/local-first/src/storage-manager.ts load() deletes and raises ValidationError on schema-invalid stored data; sync-manager.ts validates before every save
scenarios.hypothesis: after a version bump, load() persists and returns initialData that violates the model schema, which the next load() will then destroy

execution.runner: scripts/run-batch.mjs (three consecutive isolated runs per scenario via the run-scenario contract)

contamination_notes: the generation context read the seed PR (#129) and the rejected seed PR (#137) by design, and clean module sources at the pinned revision

the generation context never read benchmark/manifest.json; a docker image listing exposed planted-defect ids as image tag names (names only, no diffs); none of the three scenarios targets a planted defect and all runs used clean images
